chapter: Swing and what makes a band play
title: Benny Bailey versus Art Farmer
summary: He says Art Farmer could not swing like Benny Bailey, who played with his West Coast group; players fit different rhythm sections.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you, I'll say this. Now you've heard Benny Bailey play.
Benny Bailey. And you've heard Art Farmer play.
Art Farmer cannot swing like Benny Bailey.
There's not a chance in the world. With all due respect to Art. Art played with the group I had over

on the coast. He played with me and his brother played with me, too, on bass. You know? But their conception -- see, here's what I mean. Speaking of conceptions, he would be better, you know what I mean, with a group that's thinking in terms of Diz and even including the bass player, drummers that think in those terms, better than put him in a group that is swinging. See? You put him in a group that's swinging, he's lost. But you put him in a technical group, he's at home.
You put a technical cat over here where they're swinging --
But if you put -- you have Lester in Basie's band and then you have Lester ten years later with some of these bad rhythm sections, you can't expect him to play the same thing.
That's right. You can't expect him.
